classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the regular octagon's vertices as concyclic, identify the common intercepted arc, and convert its two side intervals into a central and then inscribed angle.

content.prompt: A regular octagon is shown below. Explain why each of the angles shown below are the same, and find their measure.

spec.description: Regular octagon with top and bottom vertices. The five upper-boundary vertices each connect to both lower side vertices; boundary sides supply the two outer connections. Decorative cyan fill is omitted.
spec.mathematics: The five inscribed angles stand on the same arc between the lower-left and lower-right vertices, passing through the bottom vertex.
spec.answerVisibility: No angle values, circumcircle or construction radii are supplied.

answer.short:
Each angle is $45^\circ$.

They intercept the same arc, whose central angle is $90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The vertices of a regular octagon lie on a circle. Each indicated angle intercepts the same arc between the lower-left and lower-right vertices, so the angles are equal.

Each side subtends $360^\circ\div8=45^\circ$ at the centre. The common arc spans two sides, so its central angle is $2\times45^\circ=90^\circ$. Each inscribed angle is therefore $\tfrac12\times90^\circ=45^\circ$.
